items.title: How AI Made Me a Better Photographer (Not Replaced Me)
items.summary:
What if AI isn't here to replace photographers, but to unlock unprecedented creative freedom? Join me on a deeply personal journey as I share how artificial intelligence is transforming my photography for the better, not the worse.

Discover a new perspective on AI photography in this video, where I delve into the positive impact of artificial intelligence on the modern photographic art form. From exploring the rich history of photography to demonstrating how AI can be integrated artistically and non-invasively into your creative process, I share my personal hopes and experiences. Learn how AI tools can enhance your vision, stay true to the original image, and truly elevate your work, ensuring photography remains an authentic expression of art and creativity.

items.title: Trends and Outlook for the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry's AI Policy
items.summary:
Amid the advancing AI revolution, the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry launched the “GENIAC” project in February last year. Through initiatives such as computational resource procurement support, promoting data utilization, and community activities, it is working to enhance Japan's generative AI development capabilities and advance their societal implementation. This presentation will introduce the background, content, and future outlook of these policies.

--

AI革命が進む中、経済産業省では、昨年2月に「GENIAC」プロジェクトを立ち上げ、計算資源の調達支援やデータの利活用促進、コミュニティ活動等を通じて、日本の生成AI開発力の底上げと社会実装を進めています。本講演では、こうした政策の背景や内容、今後の展望についてご紹介します。

items.title: How the Briefcase Technique Helps You Get Hired
items.summary:
In episode 947 of the SuperDataScience podcast, Jeffrey Li details the "Briefcase Technique" for job hunting. He shares an example of how he applied this at DoorDash by identifying the company's pain points and creating a detailed document outlining specific solutions. He explains that this method shifts the dynamic from a standard interview to demonstrating immediate value to the hiring manager.

Additional materials: https://www.superdatascience.com/947

items.title: FIRE all AI Agents! New SCALING Laws (Google, MIT)
items.summary:
New research from Google DeepMind & MIT proves that the "More Agents = Better" heuristic is mathematically wrong. We analyze their study of 180 agent architectures to find the "Tool-Coordination Trade-off" and why independent agent swarms amplify errors by 17.2x. 

Technical note: To keep the narrative fluid, I presented a simplified, conceptual form of the new scaling law. However, for those conducting real research in agent orchestration, the pre-print defines a more advanced, rigorous mathematical functional form (!) in Equation 1 (Page 16) and calculates critical coefficients in Table 4 (Page 19). For max performance use the extended mathematical formulae from the pre-print. 

All rights w/ authors:

items.summary_html:
New research from Google DeepMind & MIT proves that the "More Agents = Better" heuristic is mathematically wrong. We analyze their study of 180 agent architectures to find the "Tool-Coordination Trade-off" and why independent agent swarms amplify errors by 17.2x. 

Technical note: To keep the narrative fluid, I presented a simplified, conceptual form of the new scaling law. However, for those conducting real research in agent orchestration, the pre-print defines a more advanced, rigorous mathematical functional form (!) in Equation 1 (Page 16) and calculates critical coefficients in Table 4 (Page 19). For max performance use the extended mathematical formulae from the pre-print.
